title: How Rocks Put Fossils in Order

scenes.tts: How can a whale with legs be older than a whale built for open water? Imagine a cliff that holds both kinds of fossil, then read its layers like a record of events.
scenes.caption: How can a whale with legs be older than a whale built for open water? Imagine a cliff that holds both kinds of fossil, then read its layers like a record of events.
scenes.visual: COLOR MAP FOR BOTH FILMS: rock layers grey, fossils gold, volcanic ash red, DNA blue, anatomy green, development teal, tree white. A full-height schematic coastal cliff rises while two gold whale-fossil silhouettes appear in separate layers. Slow waves move at its base.
scenes.narration: How can a whale with legs be older than a whale built for open water? Imagine a cliff that holds both kinds of fossil, then read its layers like a record of events.

scenes.visual: Keep the cliff dimly visible. Place the title large over its center, then dissolve the title back into the same cliff.

scenes.tts: A fossil is preserved evidence of past life, such as a bone, shell, tooth, or footprint. Watch sediment bury one fossil, settle, then bury another. The lower layer formed before the layer above it.
scenes.caption: A fossil is preserved evidence of past life, such as a bone, shell, tooth, or footprint. Watch sediment bury one fossil, settle, then bury another. The lower layer formed before the layer above it.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the cliff. Grey sediment sweeps across the frame in three moving layers, burying one large gold fossil and later a second. Label the finished diagram 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: A fossil is preserved evidence of past life, such as a bone, shell, tooth, or footprint. Watch sediment bury one fossil, settle, then bury another. The lower layer formed before the layer above it.

scenes.tts: That order is relative dating. It tells which layer is older, without giving an age in years. In an undisturbed stack, lower layers formed first. The time arrow points upward toward younger rock.
scenes.caption: That order is relative dating. It tells which layer is older, without giving an age in years. In an undisturbed stack, lower layers formed first. The time arrow points upward toward younger rock.
scenes.visual: Carry the same stack. Grow a white time arrow beside it from bottom to top. Move the labels 'older' and 'younger' to opposite ends while sediment grains continue drifting.
scenes.narration: That order is relative dating. It tells which layer is older, without giving an age in years. In an undisturbed stack, lower layers formed first. The time arrow points upward toward younger rock.

scenes.tts: The fossil record is every fossil found so far, arranged by age. It shows kinds of life appearing, changing, and often going extinct. One cliff holds only a small piece of that record.
scenes.caption: The fossil record is every fossil found so far, arranged by age. It shows kinds of life appearing, changing, and often going extinct. One cliff holds only a small piece of that record.
scenes.visual: Transform the cliff into one page of a large schematic book. Several other grey pages slide behind it. Gold fossil silhouettes change gradually across three visible pages, and one branch ends without an extinction label.
scenes.narration: The fossil record is every fossil found so far, arranged by age. It shows kinds of life appearing, changing, and often going extinct. One cliff holds only a small piece of that record.

scenes.tts: Now the cliff tilts, and one block turns almost upside down. Which fossil is older after the rocks move? Follow the matching layers, not simply the bottom edge.
scenes.caption: Now the cliff tilts, and one block turns almost upside down. Which fossil is older after the rocks move? Follow the matching layers, not simply the bottom edge.
scenes.visual: Return to the cliff. Tip the whole stack, then rotate one fault-bounded block farther. Keep gold fossils attached to their layers, and give each grey layer its own texture so matching layers can be followed. Add one large question mark and subtle moving dust.
scenes.narration: Now the cliff tilts, and one block turns almost upside down. Which fossil is older after the rocks move? Follow the matching layers, not simply the bottom edge.

scenes.visual: Hold the tilted and rotated blocks with the question visible. Let dust drift and pulse the outlines of the two candidate layers slowly.

scenes.tts: Tilting changes the angle, not the order of formation. Folding, flipping, or faults can move old rock above young rock. Geologists reconstruct the stack before using the lower-means-older rule.
scenes.caption: Tilting changes the angle, not the order of formation. Folding, flipping, or faults can move old rock above young rock. Geologists reconstruct the stack before using the lower-means-older rule.
scenes.visual: Trace matching grey layer edges across the moved blocks, then animate the blocks back to their reconstructed positions. The time arrow returns only after the layers align. Blue, green, and teal empty evidence lanes begin growing beside it.
scenes.narration: Tilting changes the angle, not the order of formation. Folding, flipping, or faults can move old rock above young rock. Geologists reconstruct the stack before using the lower-means-older rule.

scenes.tts: Relative order is not an age. Radioactive dating adds ages in years to certain minerals. Starting atoms change into product atoms at a steady rate. Their measured amounts estimate when the mineral formed.
scenes.caption: Relative order is not an age. Radioactive dating adds ages in years to certain minerals. Starting atoms change into product atoms at a steady rate. Their measured amounts estimate when the mineral formed.
scenes.visual: A red ash layer grows across the carried cliff. Beside it, a schematic bar slowly changes from a red 'starting atoms' block into a white 'product atoms' block. Do not draw atoms or bonds.
scenes.narration: Relative order is not an age. Radioactive dating adds ages in years to certain minerals. Starting atoms change into product atoms at a steady rate. Their measured amounts estimate when the mineral formed.

scenes.tts: Watch two volcanic ash layers close around one fossil layer. The lower ash formed earlier, and the upper ash formed later. Their dates bracket the fossil, but neither gives its exact age.
scenes.caption: Watch two volcanic ash layers close around one fossil layer. The lower ash formed earlier, and the upper ash formed later. Their dates bracket the fossil, but neither gives its exact age.
scenes.visual: Add a second red ash band above the gold fossil. On-screen date chips appear only as 'older date' and 'younger date'. Red bracket arms slide inward around the fossil layer.
scenes.narration: Watch two volcanic ash layers close around one fossil layer. The lower ash formed earlier, and the upper ash formed later. Their dates bracket the fossil, but neither gives its exact age.

scenes.tts: More often, no volcanic layer sits nearby. Scientists can match a fossil layer to dated rocks elsewhere. Index fossils help when their species lived during a known span of time.
scenes.caption: More often, no volcanic layer sits nearby. Scientists can match a fossil layer to dated rocks elsewhere. Index fossils help when their species lived during a known span of time.
scenes.visual: Split the frame into two large cliffs. A distinctive gold shell silhouette appears in one layer of each. A moving dashed line aligns those layers; only the second cliff carries a red ash band.
scenes.narration: More often, no volcanic layer sits nearby. Scientists can match a fossil layer to dated rocks elsewhere. Index fossils help when their species lived during a known span of time.

scenes.tts: The cliff is not a complete diary. Most remains rot, are eaten, or never get buried quickly. Water and sediment favor some environments over others. The fossil record is a book with many missing pages.
scenes.caption: The cliff is not a complete diary. Most remains rot, are eaten, or never get buried quickly. Water and sediment favor some environments over others. The fossil record is a book with many missing pages.
scenes.visual: Transform the two cliffs back into the schematic record book. Several blank gaps open between pages. A forest page fades while a seafloor page receives moving sediment over a gold shell.
scenes.narration: The cliff is not a complete diary. Most remains rot, are eaten, or never get buried quickly. Water and sediment favor some environments over others. The fossil record is a book with many missing pages.

scenes.tts: Even with gaps, an ordered sequence can test a history. Older whale fossils retain legs and feet. Later forms have smaller hind limbs. The sequence shows change, not that one named fossil was the direct ancestor of the next.
scenes.caption: Even with gaps, an ordered sequence can test a history. Older whale fossils retain legs and feet. Later forms have smaller hind limbs. The sequence shows change, not that one named fossil was the direct ancestor of the next.
scenes.visual: Three gold schematic whale silhouettes rise along the time arrow, with legs gradually reduced. Place them on separate white branch tips, never in a single parent-to-child chain.
scenes.narration: Even with gaps, an ordered sequence can test a history. Older whale fossils retain legs and feet. Later forms have smaller hind limbs. The sequence shows change, not that one named fossil was the direct ancestor of the next.

scenes.tts: One line of evidence can mislead. Rocks may be disturbed, dates may only bracket, and fossils may be missing. A different method can check the same history. Independent evidence that agrees strengthens an explanation of common descent.
scenes.caption: One line of evidence can mislead. Rocks may be disturbed, dates may only bracket, and fossils may be missing. A different method can check the same history. Independent evidence that agrees strengthens an explanation of common descent.
scenes.visual: Keep the whale branches centered. Small icons for a tilted layer, red bracket, and missing page orbit on the left. A blue DNA lane begins growing on the right without revealing its result.
scenes.narration: One line of evidence can mislead. Rocks may be disturbed, dates may only bracket, and fossils may be missing. A different method can check the same history. Independent evidence that agrees strengthens an explanation of common descent.

scenes.tts: This film built a rock timeline. Bodies and inherited information can test the same branching history.
scenes.caption: This film built a rock timeline. Bodies and inherited information can test the same branching history.
scenes.visual: The grey cliff compresses into a narrow timeline beside the white whale tree. Blue, green, and teal empty lanes extend from the tree and keep moving gently, ready for later evidence.
scenes.narration: This film built a rock timeline. Bodies and inherited information can test the same branching history.

scenes.visual: Show one line only: 'Independent evidence that agrees strengthens an explanation of common descent.' Keep the whale tree faintly moving behind it.
